title: [3 of #7891] Flip the registration: `runtimeTypes` gains `object` + `permission`/`book` — whole rule families cross the publish door
body:
Programme slice of #7891 (split by the `domain:spec` seat, session `session_01Euoy6wyfzgiWtgCg4s6JK2`). Final slice — the actual strictness flip.

Blocked-by: #8308
Blocked-by: #8309

## Scope

With blocker A repaired (#8308) and the `permission`/`book` wiring in place (#8309), flip the `validateSecurityPosture` registration so the remaining rule families enforce at the runtime publish door (`runtimeTypes` gains `object`, `permission`, `book`), with pins recording each family's crossing. The ADR-0091 seed pair will already have crossed via #8307.

## Constraints (inherited from the parent, binding)

- ⛔ **No partial `security-role-word` wiring** — it judges six collections; it crosses whole or stays behind, stated explicitly either way (the #7220 failure shape is one rule id split across the wall).
- The #4001 rollout discipline applies: each step must demonstrate zero breakage empirically (shipped corpus: showcase + CRM + todo + blank), not by inference — `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.runtime-surface.test.ts` is the executable measurement to extend.
- Acceptance-surface change at the publish door ⇒ `claude-fable-5` clause applies at dispatch.

## Re-price on unblock (standard)

When #8308/#8309 close, re-verify this card's file surface on the merged ref before dispatch — the upstream landings are the most likely thing to have absorbed or reshaped this slice.

Part of #7891.
